title: Directed Hom factorization detects finite presentation of an algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $C$ a commutative $R$-algebra, in a fixed universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume that for every small nonempty directed set $I$, every directed system $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ of commutative $R$-algebras with $R$-algebra transition maps, its colimit $A=\varinjlim_i A_i$ in commutative $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and every $R$-algebra homomorphism $h:C\to A$, there are $i\in I$ and an $R$-algebra homomorphism $h_i:C\to A_i$ whose composite with $A_i\to A$ is $h$. Then $C$ is finitely presented over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], meaning that $C\cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ as an $R$-algebra for some finite $n,m$.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P$ be the set of all quotients $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/J$ with $n\ge0$ and $J$ a finitely generated ideal. Every finitely presented $R$-algebra is isomorphic to a member by its definition. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-colimit-fp-algebras-over-it] with $\Lambda=C$: the category $\mathcal J$ of these algebras equipped with an $R$-algebra map to $C$ is small and filtered, and its canonical cocone with vertex $C$ is a colimit in commutative $R$-algebras. The quotient models and their homomorphisms form sets in the fixed universe, since they are built from finite polynomial rings over $R$ and maps to $C$.

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] to $\mathcal J$ and the preceding algebra diagram. This gives a nonempty directed set $I$, algebras $B_i$ of finite presentation over $R$, transition maps, and maps $v_i:B_i\to C$ exhibiting $C$ itself as their colimit. The index is small in the same universe: the cited construction reindexes a small category by a set (its recorded declaration uses $A:\mathrm{Type}\,w$ when $\mathcal J:\mathrm{Type}\,w$). Thus this is a system to which the hypothesis of the item applies.

source.place: Tag 0032, lemma-directed-category-system, clause (1); applied as in Algebra Tag 00QN, first proof.

proof.text: Apply the assumed factorization property to this system and $h=\mathrm{id}_C$. Obtain $i\in I$ and an $R$-algebra map $u:C\to B_i$ with $v_i\circ u=\mathrm{id}_C$. Put $B=B_i$ and $v=v_i$. Both maps respect the original $R$-algebra structures.

source.place: Tag 00QO, (3) implies (1), factorization of the identity.

proof.text: Choose a finite polynomial presentation of $B$ over $R$, and denote the images of its variables by $b_1,\ldots,b_n$. Each element of $B$ is a polynomial in the $b_j$ with coefficients from $R$. Because $u$ is an $R$-algebra map, the image in $B$ of every $r\in R$ equals $u$ of its image in $C$. The same polynomials therefore show that $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ generate $B$ as a $C$-algebra via $u$. Hence $C\to B$ is of finite type. The composite $C\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{v}C$ is the identity, of finite presentation with zero variables and zero relations.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-over-finite-type-algebra] with its base ring $C$, intermediate algebra $B$ via $u$, final algebra $C$ with its identity structure, and homomorphism $v$. Its scalar compatibility is exactly $v\circ u=\mathrm{id}_C$; Step 4 gives its two finiteness hypotheses. Consequently $v:B\to C$ is of finite presentation. Now $R\to B$ is of finite presentation by construction. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] makes their composite $R\to C$ of finite presentation. This is the original structure map because $v$ is an $R$-algebra homomorphism, so the required finite polynomial presentation follows.
